details: The U.S. Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 3.75% to 4.00% on September 16, 2026, its first hike since 2023. This move signals a continued hawkish stance due to persistent inflation, with the 10-year Treasury yield nearing 5%. Higher rates typically make non-yielding assets like Bitcoin less attractive and can tighten financial conditions, although Grayscale Research suggests this is a mid-cycle adjustment with limited impact on crypto.
title: Federal Reserve Hikes Rates to 3.75%-4.00%, Maintaining Hawkish Outlook.

details: On September 18, 2026, the Bank of Japan (BoJ) increased its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25%, marking its highest level in 31 years. This decision was driven by inflation nearing the 2% target, a weak yen, and rising oil costs. Despite initial concerns that tighter monetary policy could impact global liquidity, Bitcoin surged above $77,000, suggesting the market viewed the hike as a sign of economic normalization.
title: Bank of Japan Hikes Interest Rates to 1.25%, Highest Since 1990s.

details: On September 15, 2026, the U.S. Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act, a long-awaited piece of legislation aimed at providing a clear regulatory framework for digital assets. This setback leaves the regulatory landscape in the U.S. uncertain for cryptocurrencies, though the market, including Bitcoin, largely shrugged off the news, indicating resilience.
title: U.S. Senate Blocks CLARITY Act, Leaving Crypto Regulation Unresolved.

details: On September 17, 2026, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $159 million in net inflows, with BlackRock's IBIT being a primary beneficiary. In contrast, spot Ethereum ETFs experienced their third consecutive day of net outflows, totaling around $39.24 million. This divergence indicates a continued preference for Bitcoin among institutional investors.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See Inflows While Ethereum ETFs Continue Outflow Streak.
